concepts.quote: a.length / 2, because each swap puts two elements in place
concepts.why: It uses a.length correctly as the element count. The loop bound is tied to the array's real size: each swap places two elements, so half the length is enough.
It writes a valid compound expression as the loop bound but never explains how it is evaluated or what type it has.
It uses / correctly to halve the length but never mentions that int division truncates or what happens to the middle element when the length is odd.

concepts.quote: each swap puts two elements in place
concepts.why: It ties the purpose of the swap to the reversal plan: one exchange places two elements, which sets how many times the loop must run.
